content:
Hi,

I’ve had a bunch of kernel panics while working on my drivers where the Rust parts are very hard to read, would it make sense to import the rustc-demangle crate and use it on every symbol of a stack trace?

It would make an address such as _RNvMs0_NtCsbmsJqfTZPer_6kernel9revocableINtB5_9RevocableINtNtNtB7_2io3mem5IoMemKj8_EE10try_accessCs1UaUS8VMkc3_12nintendo_otp+0x18/0x48 much more readable as <kernel[84580947f1a927f5]::revocable::Revocable<kernel[84580947f1a927f5]::io::mem::IoMem<8usize>>>::try_access+0x18/0x48.

Is there anything which could cause issues that way?
We actually already have the code required to demangle Rust symbols in the kernel tree. It's somewhere inside tools/perf.

Oh indeed, tools/perf/util/demangle-rust-v0.[ch]. It’s a C version though, is that for easier integration with the stack trace mechanism? I’ll look into where to move it so that it’s accessible both to perf and to the stack trace.
That's probably why they picked the C version, yes.

Is there anything which could cause issues that way?

We discussed doing that some years ago, and IIRC the stack trace code (the in-kernel one) is meant to be kept as simple as possible. One is expected to use scripts/decode_stacktrace.sh instead, which is where we added the demangling.
It's important that raw symbol name is available because demangling can be lossy (e.g. losing disambiguiator)
